remarks: Industries are willing to comply with regulation where the process is transparent, predictable and time-bound — the friction is less about the rules themselves and more about inconsistent application.
MPIDC officials were seen as comparatively responsive and more industry-friendly than several other departments.

findings.text: Applicants across several services, BPA included, are still asked to visit offices and submit physical documents even after uploading everything online — a gap in implementation rather than in how ABPAS itself was designed.
Site plans, building drawings and layout plans are often submitted more than once, to different departments, even where the same material has already been uploaded online.
Delays in building approvals are attributed to multiple approval levels, thin staffing in some departments, and continued manual processing despite the online system being in place.

Multiple authorities are involved — MPIDC, Urban Administration, Municipal bodies and others — with overlapping jurisdiction between them.
Heavy reliance on consultants to navigate the process was flagged as especially pronounced for BPA and Fire NOC.
Repeated, uncoordinated inspections by different departments were identified as part of the compliance burden.
Suggested reform: strengthen the Single Window System in practice and integrate approvals under MPIDC.
Suggested reform: enable inter-departmental data sharing and fully digitise the approval process end to end.
Recommended adopting joint inspections and improving staffing in departments that currently cause bottlenecks.

deemedApproval.text: No formal deemed-approval clause currently exists for CTO — there is no automatic approval if the statutory timeline lapses. A 'Uniform Consent' guideline from last year allows MSME units in notified industrial areas a self-certification-style pathway, but it still requires fee payment and Board processing, so it is not yet a complete deemed-approval mechanism.

validity.text: CTO is granted for a validity period of 5 years, after which the unit must apply for renewal (RCTO).

fees.text: Fee is not a flat amount; it is a slab-based figure computed on the gross capital investment of the unit, supported by a CA certificate, so cost differs between MSMEs and larger units. Where an application is rejected due to an applicant-side deficiency, the fee already deposited is retained by the Board and adjusted against a future application rather than refunded.

ed.location: Crystal IT Park, Khandwa road, Indore
ed.designation: Chief Chemist, Madhya Pradesh Pollution Control Board (MPPCB)

remarks: This discussion formed part of the wider Cost of Regulation (CoR) 2.0 survey exercise covering 26 identified services, and was conducted offline with a Regional Officer of the Madhya Pradesh Pollution Control Board.

findings.text: The entire CTE-to-CTO journey has been online and faceless since the portal went live in 2011; no physical visit is needed even for scrutiny or certificate collection.
SMS/WhatsApp-based query and fee-payment notifications, together with barcode-enabled digital certificates, have cut down turnaround time for communication and certificate delivery.
The statutory timeline has been progressively tightened over the years — from 45 days to 30 days to the current 21 days — while actual disposal has improved further to 15–20 days.

A dedicated support desk (a staff member deputed at the MPIDC office) and regular seminars/workshops help first-time and MSME applicants who would otherwise depend on paid consultants. The Board also publishes daily data on applications received.

The largest driver of delay beyond the achievable 5–10 day floor sits on the applicant's side: many units, particularly smaller ones, do not have pollution-control equipment finalised or correctly proposed at application time, requiring the Board to issue directions and wait for a revised proposal.

The relative cost of compliance is disproportionately higher for MSMEs: an ETP costing about ₹3 lakh works out to roughly 30% of a small unit's ₹15 lakh project cost, against only about 3% for a large unit with a project cost of ₹1 crore or more.
No formal deemed-approval clause currently exists for CTO; there is no automatic approval if the statutory timeline lapses.

The portal cannot distinguish between government-allotted and private land at the point of application, so this check is still made manually rather than through system validation, even though auto-fetching such records is technically feasible.
Explore system-level auto-validation of government land-allotment records from MPIDC to remove the manual land-document check in such cases.
Introduce an in-portal grievance-redressal module; escalation is currently limited to e-mail and phone contact with regional offices.
Build structured, mandatory pre-application guidance for MSME applicants on pollution-control-equipment requirements, to reduce query cycles and shorten average disposal time.
Formalise a deemed-approval clause for Green/White category units where the statutory timeline lapses, building on the existing MSME self-certification pathway.
Expedite the planned migration to the unified CPCB portal to bring pan-India standardisation to the process.

Units are classified Red, Orange, Green or White per CPCB norms based on pollution potential; this already drives statutory processing timeline and renewal validity, and could be extended to also differentiate inspection frequency and documentation depth by category.

Where an application is rejected on account of an applicant-side deficiency, the fee already deposited is not refunded — it is retained by the Board and can be adjusted against a future application by the same applicant.
CTO is valid for 5 years, after which the unit must apply for renewal (RCTO).

gaps.text: No deemed-approval clause exists for CTO; the interview does not describe any consequence or safeguard if the Board itself exceeds the statutory timeline.
Fee is described only as 'slab-based on gross capital investment' with no actual fee table or numeric slabs given.
Process has been fully online/faceless since 2011, with SMS/WhatsApp notifications and barcode-enabled digital certificate delivery requiring no physical office visit.
Statutory timeline progressively tightened from 45 to 30 to 21 days, with actual disposal running further ahead at 15–20 days.
Recommended introducing an in-portal grievance-redressal module since escalation is currently limited to e-mail and phone contact with regional offices.
Recommended formalising a deemed-approval clause for Green/White category units, building on the existing MSME Uniform Consent self-certification pathway.
No breakdown given of what land-registry/diversion certificate requirements apply when land is privately held, beyond naming the document.

ed.location: Association of All Industries, Mandi deep Industrial Area, Bhopal, MP
ed.designation: Director, Madhya Pradesh Industrial Development Corporation (MPIDC)

remarks: Participants spoke positively of MPIDC's role in maintaining industrial infrastructure — roads, street lighting, drainage and water supply.
MPIDC officials were generally seen as more responsive and industry-friendly than several other departments.

findings.text: The registration leg of Land Allotment is genuinely well digitised through the Cyber Sub-Registry system, with online document upload and electronic appointment scheduling.
A video-conference-based tripartite verification is used in place of an in-person meeting, and property registration itself is executed digitally.

The broader group discussion suggests the registration leg isn't the whole picture on the ground — industries said they still run into physical document submission and in-person departmental visits more generally, even where a service is nominally online.
Identity and business documents (PAN, GST registration, Aadhaar) tend to get submitted repeatedly across services.
Documents already filed with MPIDC are sometimes asked for again by the Registration Department and other authorities.
Multiple departments are involved — MPIDC, the Registration Department and the Sampada portal — resulting in a fragmented overall process for transferring industrial plots.
Duplicate fees and taxes were flagged as a recurring issue during land transfers, including duplicate stamp duty and registration-related charges.
Existing land allotment norms are seen as allowing speculative acquisition of plots, limiting access for genuine entrepreneurs.
The group discussion flagged inconsistent recognition and implementation of deemed approval provisions as a cross-cutting issue, Land Allotment included.
Suggested reforms: simplify land transfer procedures and resolve the duplicate stamp duty and registration issue.
Further suggested reforms: integrate departments and enable data sharing, minimise physical interaction, and strengthen the Single Window System.
Recommended implementing deemed approval provisions effectively, rather than leaving them as policy on paper.
Recommended reviewing eligibility norms to guard against speculative plot acquisition and improve access for genuine entrepreneurs.
MPIDC's digital Land Allotment process is regarded as among the leading practices of its kind in India.

MPIDC officials were generally seen as more responsive and industry-friendly than several other departments, and participants spoke positively of MPIDC's role in maintaining industrial infrastructure.

The expert describes the registration leg as 'genuinely well digitised' with reduced need for repeat physical visits, while the same report's broader group discussion states industries still run into physical document submission and in-person visits generally — flagged in the document itself as a stakeholder-experience gap rather than a contradiction.
Letter of Intent issued within 7 days functions as a deemed approval; tripartite video conferencing replaces physical meetings for registration verification.
Recommended integrating departments with genuine data sharing, minimising physical interaction, and reviewing eligibility norms against speculative plot acquisition.

ed.location: Crystal IT Park, Khandwa Road, Indore
ed.designation: Chief Chemist, Madhya Pradesh Pollution Control Board (MPPCB)

remarks: Renewal-related queries formed the concluding part of a broader discussion on the Consent to Establish/Operate lifecycle, held offline under the Cost of Regulation (CoR) 2.0 survey exercise with a Regional Officer of the Madhya Pradesh Pollution Control Board.

findings.text: An auto-renewal facility is already operational for Green category units, cutting both documentation and turnaround time.
The renewal timeline has followed the same downward trend as CTO — from 45, to 30, to the current 21 days statutorily — with 15–20 days achieved in practice.
WhatsApp/SMS-based fee and certificate delivery, with barcode, applies equally to renewal, removing the need for any physical office visit.
No deemed-approval clause exists specifically for renewal, though the Green-category auto-renewal facility functions as a de facto near-automatic route.

Applicants are currently asked to reference/resubmit the same documents already available with the Board from the earlier CTO, even though these could in principle be auto-fetched internally except where an actual change (such as expansion) has occurred.
As with fresh CTO, delays mostly stem from the applicant's own preparedness, particularly where an expansion triggers a fresh proposal-and-review cycle for pollution-control arrangements.
Extend the auto-renewal facility, currently limited to Green category units, to other low-risk categories with a clean compliance record (e.g. well-performing Orange units).
Enable system-level auto-fetch of previously submitted CTO documents for renewal cases with no material change, rather than requiring the applicant to reference/resubmit them.
Publish a clear, category-wise renewal validity and fee schedule on the portal, so applicants know upfront which validity period (5/10/15 years) and fee slab applies to them.
Introduce a structured in-portal grievance mechanism for renewal applications, mirroring the recommendation made for fresh CTE/CTO.
Continue and expedite migration to the unified CPCB portal for pan-India consistency in renewal processing.

The Red/Orange/Green/White classification directly determines renewal validity (up to 15 years for Green, shorter for higher-risk categories) and also underpins the Green-category auto-renewal facility.
Simple amendments such as correcting a typographical error or a name change without a director change attract no fee; a fee applies only where directors change, which must be intimated within a year.

gaps.text: No deemed-approval clause exists for renewal specifically; the interview does not describe any consequence or safeguard if the statutory renewal timeline lapses outside the Green-category auto-renewal route.
Fee is described only as the 'same fee structure as fresh CTO — slab-based' with no numeric slabs given for renewal.
Auto-renewal facility already operational for Green category units, cutting documentation and turnaround time; WhatsApp/SMS barcode-based certificate delivery removes the need for a physical visit.

Recommended extending the auto-renewal/minimal-documentation route to other low-risk categories, enabling system-level auto-fetch of previously submitted documents, publishing a clear validity/fee schedule, and adding an in-portal grievance mechanism.
